description:
Over the capture the downlink reference signal power improved early, rising by 11.22 dB to a peak of −87.00 dB; across the trace RSRP ranged from −98.2 dB to −87.0 dB. The average RSRP was −88.1 dB. Uplink SNR showed a strong rise (about 15.78 dB) to a high near 21.45 dB; UL_SNR over the period spanned 5.7 dB to 22.2 dB, with a mean of 20.7 dB.  

Uplink modulation was consistently high: UL_MCS varied between 26.0 and 27.0 with a mean of 27.0, while DL_MCS stayed constant at 7.0. Downlink BLER remained very low, between 0 and 0.017 with a mean of 0.0016. Uplink BLER fell during the trace to a low of 0.04; overall UL_BLER ranged from 0.023 to 0.2 and averaged 0.062.

Resource usage was modest. Allocated uplink PRBs ranged from 5.0 to 18.1 with a mean of 6.0. Current downlink PRBs varied between 0 and 7.9, mean 1.6; current uplink PRBs varied between 0 and 2.5, mean 0.2. DL PRB utilization ranged 0 to 7.4 with a mean of 1.5, and UL PRB utilization ranged 0 to 2.4 with a mean of 0.19. Packet counts were low-to-moderate: UL packets 0–14 (mean 2.9) and DL packets 0–19 (mean 5.4).

Throughput and buffers were intermittent. Transmitted bytes ranged from 0 to 29,000 Bytes with a mean of 7,391.4 Bytes; received bytes ranged from 71 to 21,021 Bytes with a mean of 761.6 Bytes. The estimated uplink buffer varied between 25.3 and 3,255.8 Kilobytes and averaged 741.0 Kilobytes.

Traffic was predominantly TCP: downlink used TCP for 85.94% of timestamps (UDP 0.78%), and uplink used TCP for 82.81% (UDP 1.56%). Overall the session shows improving RF conditions (notably UL_SNR and RSRP increases), high uplink MCS, low DL BLER, modest PRB utilization, and generally TCP-dominated traffic.

anomalies.troubleshooting_tickets:

- **Symptoms:** Significant decreases in reference signal received power (8–15 dB), uplink signal-to-noise ratio (8–15 dB), transmitted/received bytes (30–80%), and uplink/downlink packet counts (40–70%); increased uplink/downlink block error rates (50–200%), PRB utilization (30–80%), and PRB allocations (20–70%).
- **Root Cause:** Overlapping frequency channels between neighboring cells causing interference.
- **Resolution:** Reconfigured channel allocations to minimize overlap, optimized frequency planning, and adjusted power levels to reduce interference.
